headline: BULLISH
headline_tag: long-run uptrend holds, but price sits right on its key floor

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's long-run posture is still to grow acquisition, because the 3-6 month uptrend holds, but today it should be applied carefully. A Rally watch drop window opened yesterday, Bitcoin is down about 11% in a month, and price sits only about 1% above its 200-day average ($73,101). In practice: keep acquisition running in small, easy-to-pause steps, hold trader-targeted promotions and keep a budget reserve, and lead with trust and education. Step up only after a close back above $80,937 (the 50-day average); a close under $73,101 is the cue to shift budget toward keeping existing users. This is a budget posture, not trading advice.

reasons: BTC ($74,045) is only about 1% above its 200-day average ($73,101), which is still rising.
Up about 18% over 90 days; about 96% of those days closed above the long-term average.
But down about 11% in 30 days; 22 days under the 50-day average ($80,937).
Fear & Greed at 28 (fear); MSCI dropping Strategy and a likely December Fed hike weigh on the month.
watch: Bitcoin is sitting about 1% above its 200-day average, the main line holding up the long-run uptrend, while a Rally watch drop window is open and a December Fed rate rise looks likely. A close below $73,101 would put that uptrend in question, while a close back above $75,750 would ease the pressure.
analysis: Bottom line: the long-run uptrend still holds, but the coming week looks soft and Bitcoin is sitting just above the line that matters most. At about $74,045 it has closed under its 50-day average for 22 days, sits about 9% below it and about 12% below its 30-day high, and Fear & Greed reads 28 (fear); a Rally watch drop window opened yesterday. A normal week swings about $3,492, so a close above $75,750 (top of a typical week's swing) would ease the pressure, a close below $73,796 (the 30-day low) would turn the week clearly down, and in between it stays choppy. This is a week for calm, safety-first messaging rather than promotions.

The next month is mixed and leaning softer. The 90-day numbers still point up, with price about 18% higher and about 96% of those days closing above the long-term average, but the last 30 days are down about 11%, and news is taking some more off: MSCI said it will drop Strategy and Metaplanet from its global indexes after 30 November, and a December Fed rate rise is now described as all but certain (PANews). Price must win back $80,937 (the 50-day average) for the month to firm up, and only above $86,603 (the 90-day high) is there real room to climb; while it stays under that average, the month keeps fading, so hold bigger campaign pushes.

The 3-6 month picture still leans up at a moderate strength. Price is only about 1% above its 200-day average, which is still rising about 5% over 90 days, and news is adding a little: Russia's central bank said its exchanges may start crypto trading from 22 November and Deutsche Bank launched crypto custody for institutions (PANews). The recovery stays intact while price holds above $73,101 (the 200-day average); if that goes, $67,931 (the 200-week average) is the next floor, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. A close below the 200-day average would weaken this picture and be the moment to shift budget toward keeping existing users.
